summary: Unexpected surge of 5xx errors during route-weight rebalance coincident with tenant embedding burst
description: Customer reports a sudden increase in 5xx responses (predominantly 502/503) for short-lived streaming sessions and small-batch embedding requests starting around 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC. The timing aligns with a weighted-route adjustment deployment targeted at balancing traffic across replicas. Errors started as a small spike and escalated to a sustained elevated error rate for ~45 minutes affecting multiple tenants but primarily LexiSearch, which was performing a high-frequency embedding upload job during the window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs concurrent embedding upload job (batch size 64, 8 parallel workers) against /v1/embeddings endpoint
2) Platform performs a route-weight rebalance across runtimes to shift 20% traffic to warm spare pool
3) Short-lived streaming sessions and embedding batches begin encountering 502/503 responses after TCP handshakes succeed
4) Errors observed escalate when KV cache miss rate increases and runtime prefetch thrashing is visible
logs: [2026-03-11T02:10:46Z] runtime-serve: accept fd 19234 -> spawn worker pid=1287, model=embedder-open-v2
[2026-03-11T02:11:03Z] runtime-serve: kvcache: shard=13 miss_rate=0.72, prefetch=throttle, evict_rate=0.60
[2026-03-11T02:11:10Z] apigw: upstream_reset for conn_id=0x7f9a, returned 502 (upstream unhealthy) count=31 in 60s
[2026-03-11T02:12:05Z] runtime-monitor: gpu_util spike=96%, mem_frag=28%, watchdog_kill=0 (soft-retries); several runtimes reported short OOM-reclaim cycles
comments: 2026-03-11 02:22 - Aisha Thompson (Support): Received initial report from LexiSearch CS rep. Confirmed elevated 5xx rate and collected logs. Escalating to SRE and Runtime team.
2026-03-11 02:30 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Noted route-weight rebalance at 02:10 UTC. Querying autoscaler and prefetch stats. Requested customer to pause embedding job to test error drain.
2026-03-11 02:37 - LexiSearch (Customer): Paused upload job at 02:35 UTC. Error rate dropped but a residual 5xx floor persisted (~1-2%). Customer asks for timeline and whether data was lost.

2026-03-11 03:05 - Runtime Eng (Elena Park): Observed kvcache shard hotness on nodes receiving shifted traffic. Prefetch threads saturated causing request latency and some upstream resets. Proposing quick mitigation: adjust route-weight rollback and temporarily increase kvcache concurrency on target pool.

2026-03-11 03:18 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Performed rollback of route-weight change at 03:12 UTC and scaled kvcache concurrency to 1.5x on affected nodes. 5xx rate fell to baseline by 03:22 UTC for most tenants; LexiSearch reported full recovery after resuming uploads at 03:40 UTC.
2026-03-12 09:12 - Product Ops (Grace Liu): Requested post-incident analysis for onboarding safeguards to avoid route changes during heavy embedding jobs. Adding to follow-up items.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: route-weight rebalance moved a concentrated tenant workload to a smaller set of warm spares that had cold KV-cache state, triggering prefetch storms and high miss rates.
Correlated metrics: kvcache miss rate jumped from 0.05 -> 0.72 on affected nodes; apigw accept_queue length increased and upstream reset counts rose concurrently.
Observed that embedding job from LexiSearch had many small parallel connections with short lifetimes, which increased connection churn and prevented KV warmup on the new targets.
Runtime logs show repeated prefetch attempts and eviction loops, causing CPU stalls on runtime proxy threads and amplifying hedged retries from apigw, resulting in 502/503s.
No evidence of persistent data loss; requests that returned 5xx were not persisted — customer retried successfully after recovery.
Related internal ticket INT-7782 opened to track autoscaler/route policy improvement and protective gating around tenant heavy-upload windows.
Temporary mitigation turned out effective: rollback route-weight change + increase kvcache concurrency + request customer to pause heavy job during mitigation.
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-11 03:12 UTC: rolled back route-weight change and increased kvcache concurrency on affected pool. Monitoring until stable metrics observed.
Customer confirmed recovery by 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC after resuming their job; no lost data reported.

Follow-ups issued: INT-7782 (route-change gating), create a runbook item to detect ongoing high-concurrency embedding uploads before automated route rebalances, and add telemetry alert for kvcache miss_rate > 0.25 during rebalancing.

Permanent remediation plan: implement a short quiesce window to avoid weight changes while a tenant has active high-concurrency small-connection workloads, and tune prefetch backoff to be more conservative when miss spikes are detected.
Status: monitoring and actionable follow-ups assigned to Runtime and Routing teams (owners: Elena Park, routing; Priya Nair, runtime).
